ask: Can you give this session a read-only key for the Cloudflare server logs?
problem: One person on the web app saw two reference-audio downloads fail with a server error. We still do not know why.
found: The 502 answers come from the web server, whose logs live in Cloudflare. This session has no key for them, and I may not read secrets. The phone data needs its own key too.
why: A read-only key lets me check the logs without changing anything. The audio failures are not in the Supabase logs, so that link alone will not help.
touches: Nothing else. I would only read, never write.
steps: In Cloudflare, create an API token that can only read Workers logs (Workers Observability, read).
In this cloud session's settings, add api.cloudflare.com as a connected service with that token, so I never see it.
Optional: connect the Supabase connector in your Claude settings so I can read the person's timeline.
